note: The module ships exactly one Search API processor plugin, id `html_element_filter` (class HtmlElementFilter extends FieldsProcessorPluginBase). It removes DOM elements matching CSS selectors from field markup before indexing (stage preprocess_index) and optionally from result item fields (stage postprocess_query, controlled by boolean enable_postprocess_query, default TRUE). Settings live only on the host index config entity: search_api.index.<id> -> processor_settings.html_element_filter.{css_selectors (newline-separated string), enable_postprocess_query}. No configure route, no permissions, no Drush, no config of its own. Medium/hard cases are grounded in a real namespaced index (sahef_*) whose processor_settings are read/written on the live site.

evals.prompt: I want a Search API processor that deletes certain HTML elements from content before it gets indexed. What is the machine name (plugin id) of the processor that the search_api_html_element_filter module provides, and what does it do?
evals.expected_output: The processor plugin id is html_element_filter (class HtmlElementFilter, extends FieldsProcessorPluginBase). Add it to an index and give it CSS selectors; it removes matching elements from field markup before indexing.

evals.prompt: How do I tell the search_api_html_element_filter processor which elements to strip, and how are multiple selectors entered? Name the setting keys it stores.
evals.expected_output: It stores css_selectors (a textarea of CSS selectors, one per line, split on \r\n) and enable_postprocess_query (boolean, default TRUE). Enter each selector such as .sidebar-filters or .advert on its own line.

evals.prompt: At which Search API processing stages does the html_element_filter processor act, what library does it use to parse and remove the HTML, and what does the 'Enable post-process query' option change?
evals.expected_output: It runs at preprocess_index (strip before indexing) and, when Enable post-process query (enable_postprocess_query) is on, at postprocess_query (strip the same elements from returned result item fields). Parsing/removal uses Symfony DomCrawler with CssSelector.

evals.prompt: This site has a Search API index named sahef_index that uses the HTML Element Filter processor. Inspect the live index configuration and state the CSS selector it is configured to strip from content.
evals.expected_output: search_api.index.sahef_index processor_settings.html_element_filter.css_selectors is '.sidebar-filters'. Read with `drush cget search_api.index.sahef_index processor_settings.html_element_filter`.

evals.prompt: This site has a Search API index named sahef_pp that uses the HTML Element Filter processor. Inspect the live index configuration and state whether the processor's 'Enable post-process query' option (which also strips the elements from returned search results) is turned on or off for that index.
evals.expected_output: It is OFF: in search_api.index.sahef_pp, processor_settings.html_element_filter.enable_postprocess_query is FALSE, so the elements are stripped only at index time, not from result items. Read with `drush cget search_api.index.sahef_pp processor_settings.html_element_filter`.

evals.prompt: This site has a Search API index with machine name sahef_task that currently does NOT use the HTML Element Filter processor. Enable the search_api_html_element_filter processor (html_element_filter) on that index and configure it to strip elements matching the CSS selector .advert. Apply the change to the live index configuration.
evals.expected_output: In search_api.index.sahef_task, processor_settings.html_element_filter is present with css_selectors containing .advert (e.g. via the Processors UI, $index->addProcessor(), or editing processor_settings in config).

evals.prompt: On my search index (machine name sahef_task), the little filter widget boxes that use the CSS class 'sidebar-filters' keep showing up in my search results text. Make the search stop indexing anything inside elements with the class sidebar-filters, and save it to the site.
evals.expected_output: In search_api.index.sahef_task, processor_settings.html_element_filter is present with css_selectors containing .sidebar-filters (add the HTML Element Filter processor and set the selector to .sidebar-filters).
